text: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did is what I call the arrogant doctor.
speaker: Andy Raskin
context: Andy introduces his background and explains how he discovered a different approach to pitching. He contrasts the traditional business school method (which he calls the 'arrogant doctor' approach) with the storytelling structure he learned from screenwriting books. The 'arrogant doctor' method focuses on presenting problems and solutions, while his preferred approach starts by establishing a fundamental shift happening in the world - from an old way of doing things to a new way.
text_ko: 제가 비즈니스 스쿨에서 배운 피칭 방식, 그리고 아마 대부분이 배운 방식은 제가 '거만한 의사(arrogant doctor)'라고 부르는 거예요.
text_zh: 我在商学院学的那套路演方法，我觉得大部分人学的都是这样，我叫它"傲慢医生"模式。
text_es: La forma en que me enseñaron a presentar en la escuela de negocios, y creo que a la mayoría, es lo que yo llamo el doctor arrogante.
key_sentence: what I call the arrogant doctor.
original_text: The way I learned how to pitch in business school, and I think the way most people did is what I call the arrogant doctor. So you have a problem, a pain, I have a solution, a treatment, and I'm going to tell you why it's better than all the other treatments. And the structure that I read about in these movies was different. Every movie starts with some kind of shift in the world, and I call this shift the shift from the old game to a new game.

vocabulary.definition: A pitch is a presentation or proposal aimed at persuading an audience to support a project, idea, or product.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, particularly in startups, a pitch is often delivered to potential investors or clients to secure funding or partnerships.
vocabulary.nuance: While a pitch can be straightforward, it often carries a connotation of being overly promotional or lacking authenticity if not delivered with genuine enthusiasm.

text: This structure really is about defining a movement, and that's very different from, 'Hey, I'm going to solve your problem.' What I think is really interesting as a kind of qualifier is that this story has a certain structure.
speaker: Andy Raskin
context: Lenny asks Andy to define what a strategic narrative is. Andy explains that it's one story that CEOs use to drive success across marketing, sales, product, fundraising, and recruiting. He emphasizes that this approach is about defining a movement rather than simply solving problems. Andy contrasts his recommended structure with the traditional 'arrogant doctor' approach where you present a problem and then explain why your solution is better than competitors.
text_ko: 이 구조(structure)는 사실 어떤 운동(movement)을 정의하는 것에 관한 거예요. 그건 ‘제가 문제를 해결해 드리겠습니다’라는 식의 접근과는 완전히 달라요. 흥미로운 건, 일종의 한정자(qualifier)로서 이 이야기가 특정한 구조(structure)를 가지고 있다는 점이에요.
text_zh: 这个框架其实是在定义一种运动，这和"嘿，我来帮你解决问题"完全不是一回事。我觉得特别有意思的一点是，这个故事本身就有一定的结构在里面。
text_es: Esta estructura realmente se trata de definir un movimiento, y eso es muy diferente a decir 'Oye, te voy a resolver el problema.' Lo que me parece realmente interesante como una especie de filtro es que esta historia tiene una estructura particular.
key_sentence: Defining a movement differs from simply solving a problem.
original_text: This structure really is about defining a movement, and that's very different from, 'Hey, I'm going to solve your problem.' What I think is really interesting as a kind of qualifier is that this story has a certain structure. And the traditional structure, the way I learned how to pitch in business school, I think the way most people did is what I call the arrogant doctor.

vocabulary.definition: A qualifier is a word or phrase that modifies or limits the meaning of another term, often providing additional context or specificity. In a broader sense, it can refer to any condition or factor that affects the interpretation of a statement.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communication, qualifiers are used to clarify statements, manage expectations, and provide nuanced information, particularly in negotiations or presentations where precision is crucial.
vocabulary.nuance: Using qualifiers can enhance clarity, but overusing them may lead to ambiguity or weaken the impact of a statement, so they should be employed judiciously.

vocabulary.definition: Structure refers to the arrangement or organization of components within a system, which can include physical, conceptual, or procedural elements. It provides a framework that facilitates understanding and functionality.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, structure can pertain to organizational hierarchy, project management frameworks, or the design of processes, all of which are essential for ensuring efficiency and clarity in operations.
vocabulary.nuance: While structure is often associated with stability and order, it can also imply rigidity; thus, it is important to balance structure with flexibility to adapt to changing circumstances.

text: What's really, I think key is naming it, naming that old game. The examples you saw, software, cloud, transactions, subscription opinions, reality. This very, very concise naming is really key. And it's hard because in making it compact you're losing completeness.
speaker: Andy Raskin
context: Lenny asks Andy to explain the framework for strategic narratives in more detail. Andy explains that one crucial element is naming both the old game and new game very concisely - like 'software to cloud' or 'transactions to subscriptions.' He acknowledges that this compact naming requires some oversimplification and that people might challenge whether the shift is really as universal as claimed, but argues this isn't actually a problem in practice.
text_ko: 제가 보기엔 정말 핵심은 그걸 이름 붙이는 거예요, 그 오래된 게임에 이름을 붙이는 것. 보셨던 예들—소프트웨어(software), 클라우드(cloud), 거래(transactions), 구독(subscription) 같은 것들요. 이렇게 아주 간결하게 이름 붙이는 게 진짜 중요해요. 그런데 그게 어려워요. 간결하게 만들다 보면 포괄성을 잃게 되니까요.
text_zh: 我觉得关键是要给它起个名字，把那套老玩法明确定义出来。你看到的那些例子，软件啊、云服务啊、交易啊、订阅模式啊，现实情况就是这样。这种非常简洁的命名真的很关键。但难就难在，你要做得简洁，就必然会丢掉一些完整性。
text_es: Lo que realmente creo que es clave es ponerle nombre, nombrar ese juego anterior. Los ejemplos que vieron - software, nube, transacciones, suscripciones, opiniones, realidad. Ese naming tan, tan conciso es realmente clave. Y es difícil porque al hacerlo compacto pierdes completitud.
key_sentence: This very, very concise naming is really key.
original_text: What's really, I think key is naming it, naming that old game. The examples you saw, software, cloud, transactions, subscription opinions, reality. This very, very concise naming is really key. And it's hard because in making it compact you're losing completeness. So you can imagine you're in a meeting, someone says like, 'Hey, how about we do transactions to subscriptions?' And someone says, 'Well I don't know, there's a lot of things I don't really subscribe to. Subscription economy, really?' So we're always kind of overstating it in a way, but it's not a problem.

vocabulary.definition: Expressing or covering much in few words; clear and succinct.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business communications, being concise is crucial for effective presentations and reports, where clarity and brevity can enhance understanding and decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: While concise communication is valued, it should not come at the expense of important details; thus, it is essential to balance brevity with completeness.

vocabulary.definition: The state of being whole or undivided; having all necessary parts or elements.
vocabulary.businessContext: In project management and product development, completeness is vital to ensure that all aspects of a project are addressed, minimizing risks and enhancing quality.
vocabulary.nuance: While completeness is important, it can sometimes lead to analysis paralysis; thus, it is essential to find a balance between thoroughness and timely execution.

text: And whenever I work with teams and I talk about this, so they're like, 'Okay, I guess we got to then for kill the prospect's aunt and uncle,' and basically yes, I mean figuratively.
speaker: Andy Raskin
context: Andy uses a Star Wars analogy to explain how to create urgency in strategic narratives. He references how Luke Skywalker initially refuses the call to adventure until his aunt and uncle are killed, making the stakes life-and-death. Andy explains that in business pitches, you need to show prospects that their future won't be 'sort of okay' - there will be clear winners and losers based on whether they adapt to the new paradigm or stick with the old way.
text_ko: 제가 팀들과 이 얘기를 나눌 때마다 다들 “그럼 잠재고객(prospect)의 이모, 삼촌까지 없애야 한다는 건가요?” 하고 반응해요. 그리고 기본적으로, 네 — 말 그대로가 아니라 비유적으로 하는 말이에요.
text_zh: 每次我跟团队聊这个话题的时候，他们就会说，"好吧，那看来我们得把客户的七大姑八大姨都给'干掉'了"，我的意思当然是比喻啦。
text_es: Y cuando trabajo with equipos y les hablo de esto, me dicen: 'Bueno, entonces tenemos que matar a los tíos del prospecto,' y básicamente sí, pero en sentido figurado.
key_sentence: We must figuratively kill the prospect's aunt and uncle to show future outcomes.
original_text: And whenever I work with teams and I talk about this, so they're like, 'Okay, I guess we got to then for kill the prospect's aunt and uncle,' and basically yes, I mean figuratively. We got to show them that the future is not going to just be sort of okay. They see it as split between a very negative outcome and a potentially very positive outcome.

vocabulary.definition: In a manner that is metaphorical or symbolic rather than literal, often used to express ideas in a more imaginative way.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, using figurative language can help convey complex concepts or emotions more effectively, making them relatable to the audience.
vocabulary.nuance: While figurative language can enhance communication, it should be used carefully to ensure clarity and avoid misunderstandings, especially in formal contexts.

text: It becomes the strategic north star for the product.
speaker: Andy Raskin
context: Lenny asks about the impact Andy has seen from companies shifting to his strategic narrative approach. Andy explains that beyond helping with sales and marketing, the strategic narrative becomes a decision-making framework for product development. A CEO Andy recently interviewed explained that they were constantly receiving feature requests from sales and customer success teams but had no clear criteria for prioritization until they developed their strategic narrative, which now serves as their filter for what features to build.
text_zh: 这就成了产品的战略指南针。
text_es: Se convierte en la brújula estratégica del producto.
key_sentence: It becomes the strategic north star for the product.
original_text: Another thing I just hear always, I just interviewed a CEO this morning for my podcast and this is the first thing he actually said was, 'It becomes the strategic north star for the product.' So what he was telling me, and this was actually a little unusual, I asked him, 'Why did you come to me at first?' And of course I'd asked him that before, but he said something this time that was a little different from what I'd heard before. He said, 'We are constantly getting feature requests through sales, through customer success. And we had sort of no way, bar to decide well what do we take on, what don't we take on? And this clearly has become our bar.'

vocabulary.definition: Relating to the identification of long-term or overall aims and interests and the means of achieving them.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, 'strategic' often refers to decisions or plans that are designed to achieve significant goals or competitive advantages over time.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'strategic' implies a focus on long-term planning, it should not be confused with tactical, which refers to short-term actions.

text: But I guess I feel like still by calling it category and category name, we're just focusing on those three words so much.
speaker: Andy Raskin
context: Lenny asks Andy about his perspective on category creation, noting that Andy doesn't seem to be a big fan of this popular approach. Andy explains that while he's not entirely against category creation, he believes people get too focused on finding the perfect category name (usually three words) rather than developing the underlying story. He argues that CEOs often create category names but then struggle to build a compelling narrative around them, which is why he prefers to focus on story and movement creation first.
text_ko: 근데 '카테고리(category)'랑 '카테고리 이름(category name)'이라고만 부르다 보니, 결국 그 세 단어에만 너무 집착하는 것 같아요.
text_zh: 不过我觉得吧，咱们老是盯着"品类"和"品类名称"这几个词，可能有点钻牛角尖了。
text_es: Pero siento que al seguir llamándolo categoría y nombre de categoría, nos estamos enfocando demasiado en esas tres palabras.
key_sentence: we're just focusing on those three words so much.
original_text: But I guess I feel like still by calling it category and category name, we're just focusing on those three words so much. And what happens often is CEOs will, they'll kind of come up with this little category, like what happened with Nick at the 360Learning with collaborative learning. We have this name, but we don't know how to tell the story around it. So my feeling is like, well, let's focus on the story.

vocabulary.definition: The act of concentrating attention or resources on a specific area or objective.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, focusing is vital for prioritizing initiatives and ensuring that teams allocate their efforts towards achieving key goals effectively.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'focusing' suggests a deliberate and strategic choice, it can also imply the exclusion of other options, which may not always be favorable.

text: Well, I can tell you what I hear from CEOs when they contact me. I always ask, what's happening? Because that idea I had, no CEO's going to budget a line item for this. I'm basically asking, why was I wrong?
speaker: Andy Raskin
context: Lenny asks what signs indicate that a company should work on their strategic narrative. Andy explains that he originally thought no CEO would budget for narrative work, so he always asks CEOs why they're reaching out. One common scenario is when companies are maturing beyond the stage where success depended on the founders being directly involved in every decision - what one CEO called 'brute force of the founders' - and they need a way to scale their vision and decision-making across the growing organization.
text_ko: 음, CEO들이 저한테 연락할 때 제가 주로 듣는 얘기를 말씀드릴게요. 저는 항상 먼저 '무슨 상황인가요?'라고 물어봐요. 왜냐하면 제가 생각한 그 아이디어는 어떤 CEO도 예산 항목으로 책정하지 않을 거니까요(budget a line item). 결국 제가 묻는 건 '제가 왜 틀렸나요?'인 셈이에요.
text_zh: 我来跟你说说那些CEO联系我时都说什么。我总是会问，到底发生了什么事？因为按我原来的想法，没有哪个CEO会专门为这个事情做预算的。其实我就是想知道，我哪里判断错了？
text_es: Bueno, te puedo decir lo que escucho de los CEOs cuando me contactan. Siempre les pregunto, ¿qué está pasando? Porque esa idea que tenía yo, ningún CEO va a meter una partida en el presupuesto para esto. Básicamente les estoy preguntando, ¿en qué me equivoqué?
key_sentence: no CEO's going to budget a line item for this.
original_text: Well, I can tell you what I hear from CEOs when they contact me. I always ask, what's happening? Because that idea I had, no CEO's going to budget a line item for this. I'm basically asking, why was I wrong? So a few things they tell me, one is that the company is maturing from a point a stage where they've been successful, but that success is ... one CEO put it this way, was brute force of the founders.

vocabulary.definition: A budget is a financial plan that outlines expected revenues and expenditures over a specific period, typically used to manage resources effectively.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, budgets are crucial for financial planning, allowing organizations to allocate resources to various departments and projects while ensuring fiscal responsibility.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'budget' often refers to a formal financial plan, it can also imply constraints on spending, making it important to use in contexts where financial limitations are relevant.

vocabulary.definition: Contact refers to the act of communicating or reaching out to someone, often for the purpose of establishing a connection or exchanging information.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, making contact with clients, partners, or stakeholders is vital for networking, relationship building, and facilitating collaboration.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'contact' can imply a formal or informal interaction, and should be used in contexts where establishing a connection or communication is emphasized.
